Apply HCUP labels

Source: R/labels.R
nis_label.Rd

Apply HCUP labels

Usage

nis_label(.data)

Arguments

.data

A collected data frame.

Value

.data with binary indicators as logical, multi-level coded elements as factors, and variable labels in attr(x, "label"). Unknown codes trigger one warning per variable. They become NA in binary fields and Code <value> levels in multi-level fields. Existing variable labels are preserved. Numeric fields without a table entry are returned unchanged. The operation is idempotent.

Residence fields PL_NCHS2006, PL_NCHS, and PL_NCHS2 retain their own categories. The collapsed PL_NCHS2 uses codes 21 and 22. Code-specific labels for I10_BIRTH and I10_SERVICELINE follow HCUP's definitions.

Binary codes 0 and 1 become FALSE and TRUE, respectively. For example, FEMALE is true for female patients and AWEEKEND for weekend admissions.

Negative numeric sentinels are handled as unknown codes. The supplied HCUP documentation represents missing numeric values as system missing and does not document negative sentinels for any element handled here. NaN values in ordinary numeric vectors and Haven-labelled numeric storage are treated as missing, while ordinary and tagged NA values remain missing. Finite SPSS user-missing values and integer64 values are interpreted through their displayed values. Factors containing raw codes are normalized as a whole. Existing labels, including Code 7, are preserved when unused raw-code levels remain after subsetting. A bare Code value with raw-code levels and no recognized value label is treated as raw text; without such levels it is preserved as an existing label because its origin cannot be recovered after dropping levels.

See also

Prepare annual NIS files, Prepare annual NIS files, HCUP NIS Description of Data Elements.

Other data-access: nis_convert(), nis_example(), nis_open()

Examples

demographics <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  dplyr::select(AGE, FEMALE, RACE) |>
  dplyr::collect()
